papers_used: Schultz et al. 2021: deep learning can complement but not yet trivially replace NWP; emphasizes physical constraints and explainability limitations.
Dueben and Bauer 2018: highlights design challenges for global ML weather models, including stability, data requirements, and forecast-system design choices.
Pathak et al. 2022 (FourCastNet): demonstrates 0.25-degree high-resolution global data-driven forecasting with competitiveness against ECMWF IFS at short lead times.
Chen et al. 2023 (FengWu): transformer-based global medium-range forecasting can extend skill beyond 10 days, with lead-time-aware evaluation and multivariate design.
contract_updates: Lead-time-aware diagnostics are essential because medium-range skill decays nonlinearly.
Comparisons to ECMWF/IFS-class benchmarks should be framed cautiously when direct benchmark outputs are absent in the workspace.
Global map diagnostics and variable-specific summaries are standard artifact families for weather-AI reports.
Stability and physical plausibility should be discussed as limitations when only sample forecast artifacts are available.
